evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: This will take around ten to fifteen minutes. You can depend on this call will just take around ten to fifteen minutes. Will that work? [customer confirms 'Yeah']
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: What is your preferred move date? [Sat Sept 26 confirmed] Where are you moving from/to? [addresses obtained] Three bedroom to three bedroom, two bath [room count], estimated 2400 sq ft [approximate size]
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Before I get the details of your move, I'd like to ask what are your biggest concerns and what are the most important things you want answers to on this call today?
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises damage concern: 'I wanna make sure my furniture doesn't get damaged.' Rep responds: 'We have a no worries damage coverage' but does not ask follow-up like 'tell me more about that' or 'what specific items are you most worried about?' Moves directly to offering solution.
evidence_quotes.walkthrough_branch: Rep correctly identifies home is approximately 2400 sq ft (over 1800 threshold) and offers virtual walkthrough: 'Alternatively we can do a virtual walkthrough, it's like a video call on your preferred time and date.' Customer accepts and walkthrough is scheduled via photos/videos link.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides hourly rate ($105/mover) and explains service inclusions before customer can upload photos, but does not anchor to a typical range for a 2400 sq ft 3-bed home or personalize based on customer's stated concerns.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: No explicit ask for the business occurs; call routes cleanly to walkthrough completion with secure link sent and follow-up callback promised: 'Once I got your photos and video, I'll be giving you a callback for your personalized estimate.'

top_strength: Nicole correctly identified the move size (2,400 sq ft), recognized it required a virtual walkthrough before pricing, and cleanly routed the call to that walkthrough with a secure upload link and clear callback promise—no abandoned pitch or mid-stream confusion.
coaching_note: When the customer raised their main concern (furniture damage), Nicole jumped straight to the solution (damage coverage explanation) instead of digging deeper with a follow-up question—'tell me more about that' would have surfaced whether they were worried about specific high-value items, previous bad experiences, or something else, making the later promises land harder.
